entries.name: Complex
entries.signature: export declare class Complex { static readonly ZERO: Complex; static readonly ONE: Complex; static readonly I: Complex; readonly re: number; readonly im: number; private constructor(); /** Builds `re + im·i` from finite parts. `-0` becomes `0`. */ static fromParts(re: number, im: number): Complex; /** Converts a number, a `Complex`, or text such as `'3+4i'`, `'-2i'`, `'5'`. */ static from(value: ComplexInput): Complex; /** `r·(cos θ + i·sin θ)`. `r` must be ≥ 0; both must be finite. */ static fromPolar(r: number, theta: number): Complex; plus(other: ComplexInput): Complex; minus(other: ComplexInput): Complex; times(other: ComplexInput): Complex; /** * Robust complex division (Baudin & Smith 2012, "A Robust Complex Division * in Scilab"): Smith's algorithm, which avoids overflow in `|divisor|²`, * plus exact power-of-two scaling when a part is near overflow or underflow, * so `(1e308 + 1e308i) / (1e308 + 1e308i)` is `1`. Throws on a zero divisor, * and `NumericRangeError` only when the quotient itself is out of range. */ dividedBy(other: ComplexInput): Complex; /** `1 / z`. Throws `DivisionByZeroError` for zero. */ inverse(): Complex; negated(): Complex; /** `re - im·i`. */ conjugate(): Complex; /** * Modulus `|z|`, via `Math.hypot` so large parts do not overflow. Throws * `NumericRangeError` when `|z|` itself is beyond the float range, which * finite parts allow (up to √2 × `Number.MAX_VALUE`, as for `1e308 + 1e308i`). */ abs(): number; /** Principal argument in `(-π, π]`. The argument of zero is `0`, as in C's `carg`. */ arg(): number; /** `{ r: abs(), theta: arg() }`; throws `NumericRangeError` where `abs` does. */ toPolar(): Polar; /** `e^z`. */ exp(): Complex; /** Principal natural logarithm `ln|z| + i·arg(z)`. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` for zero. */ ln(): Complex; /** Principal logarithm in `base`: `ln(z) / ln(base)`. `base` must not be 0 or 1. */ log(base: ComplexInput): Complex; /** Principal square root: the root with `re > 0`, or `im ≥ 0` when `re` is 0. */ sqrt(): Complex; /** * Principal power `z^w = e^(w·ln z)`. An integer `w` uses repeated * multiplication (exact for small Gaussian integers); a real `w` uses polar * form (`|z|^w` at angle `w·arg z`). `0^w` is `1` for `w = 0` and `0` when * `re(w) > 0`; otherwise it throws `DivisionByZeroError`. */ pow(exponent: ComplexInput): Complex; private integerPower; /** sin(x + iy) = sin x cosh y + i cos x sinh y; overflows (`NumericRangeError`) only when the result does. */ sin(): Complex; /** cos(x + iy) = cos x cosh y − i sin x sinh y. */ cos(): Complex; /** tan z = −i·tanh(iz), by Kahan's cancellation-free formula; never overflows. */ tan(): Complex; /** sinh z = −i·sin(iz) = sinh x cos y + i cosh x sin y. */ sinh(): Complex; /** cosh z = cos(iz) = cosh x cos y + i sinh x sin y. */ cosh(): Complex; /** tanh z by Kahan's formula: (βρs + it) / (1 + βs²) with t = tan y, β = 1 + t², s = sinh x, ρ = √(1 + s²). */ tanh(): Complex; /** * Principal arcsine, real part in [-π/2, π/2]. Cuts: the real axis outside * [-1, 1]; `asin(2)` is `π/2 - 1.3170i`, `asin(-2)` is `-π/2 + 1.3170i`. */ asin(): Complex; /** * Principal arccosine, real part in [0, π]; `acos z = π/2 − asin z`, same * cuts. `acos(2)` is `1.3170i`, `acos(-2)` is `π - 1.3170i`. */ acos(): Complex; /** * Principal arctangent, real part in [-π/2, π/2]; `atan z = −i·atanh(iz)`. * Cuts: the imaginary axis outside [-i, i]; `atan(2i)` is `π/2 + 0.5493i`, * `atan(-2i)` is `-π/2 - 0.5493i`. `atan(±i)` throws `InvalidArgumentError`. */ atan(): Complex; /** * Principal inverse hyperbolic sine, `asinh z = −i·asin(iz)`. Cuts: the * imaginary axis outside [-i, i]; `asinh(2i)` is `1.3170 + π/2·i`. */ asinh(): Complex; /** * Principal inverse hyperbolic cosine, real part ≥ 0 and imaginary part in * [-π, π]. Cut: the real axis left of 1, valued from above: `acosh(0.5)` is * `1.0472i`, `acosh(-2)` is `1.3170 + πi`. */ acosh(): Complex; /** * Principal inverse hyperbolic tangent, imaginary part in [-π/2, π/2]. Cuts: * the real axis outside [-1, 1]; `atanh(2)` is `0.5493 - π/2·i`, * `atanh(-2)` is `-0.5493 + π/2·i`. `atanh(±1)` throws `InvalidArgumentError`. */ atanh(): Complex; /** * All `n` complex `n`-th roots, counter-clockwise from the principal root * (index 0, the one `pow(1/n)` returns). Zero has `n` roots, all zero. `n` above 1,000,000 throws * `ResourceLimitError`: the roots are built as objects, so `n` is bounded by memory. */ nthRoots(n: number): Complex[]; isReal(): boolean; isZero(): boolean; /** Exact equality of both parts. */ eq(other: ComplexInput): boolean; /** * `|z - w| ≤ tolerance × max(1, |z|, |w|)`: absolute near zero, relative * for large values, like `approxEqual` for numbers. */ approxEqual(other: ComplexInput, tolerance?: number): boolean; /** `3 + 4i`, `3 - 4i`, `-2i`, `i`, `5` (see the module notes for the grammar). */ toString(): string; toJSON(): string; /** Throws. A `Complex` never silently becomes a float. */ valueOf(): never; [Symbol.toPrimitive](hint: 'string' | 'number' | 'default'): string; readonly [Symbol.toStringTag] = "Complex"; }
entries.jsdocSummary: A complex number `re + im·i` with finite float parts. Create one with `complex(3, 4)`, `complex('3+4i')` or `Complex.fromPolar(r, theta)`. Equality (`eq`) is exact; use `approxEqual` after float arithmetic.
